design_questions.question: DECIDE STEP-UP: §10's sentence ('decisions require 2FA when they release a hold or keep it past 72 h (V2 SLA)') never settles the V1 rule, while the same queue family is strict (payout approve/reject always-2FA; KYC decide 2FA). Options — A: case decisions require the 2FA step-up always, from V1.0 (the D38 authz.step_up_required chain; no tier-conditional auth); B: no step-up in V1.0 (a decision is record-keeping until the hold bites), switch on with the V1.1 interlock. See docs/60 §3 F3.
design_questions.answer: **Answered 2026-09-20 — option A:** always-step-up from V1.0; risk.case.decide registered with the abac step-up clause (roles.yaml).

design_questions.question: ONE-OPEN-CASE RULE: risk.case_already_open ('second open case on same account') is a registered V1 409, but the contract flagged 'rule not in sheet' and nothing enforces it (cases key on trader with an account_ids array — no plain unique index). Options — A: per-account, app-enforced (transactional check under a per-trader advisory lock — keeps the registered meaning); B: one open case per trader (a partial unique index — simpler, but rewrites the registered code's meaning and re-keys the queue); C: no uniqueness rule in V1.0 (the 409 stays registered but never fires). See docs/60 §3 F4.
design_questions.answer: **Answered 2026-09-20 — option A:** one open case per account, transactional check under a per-trader advisory lock; documented in §3.2, §9/DDL and the contract.

design_questions.question: PAYOUT INELIGIBLE CODES: payout.ineligible carries sub-reasons from the eight PAY-03 checks, but no code scheme was ever fixed (open since the twelfth pass; the taxonomy TODO also asked whether payout.kyc_required should be a dedicated top-level code like payout.risk_hold). Options — A: a closed named enum (kyc_not_approved, min_trading_days, consistency, trading_day_threshold, first_payout_delay, next_payout_date, min_amount, max_amount, account_status, risk_hold), kyc_required stays a sub-reason — one shape for all failures; B: the enum plus a dedicated top-level 423 payout.kyc_required mirroring payout.risk_hold — two shapes for the two hard gates. See docs/62 §3.
design_questions.answer: **Answered 2026-09-20 — option A:** the closed named enum; kyc stays a sub-reason. docs/11 §6 row + api/pay.md written.

design_questions.question: METHOD CONFIRMATION (PAY-05/06, V1.1): 'save and confirm' had no defined steps and the Out-Of-Scope PAY-06 cooldown is not a V1 row (open since the twelfth pass). Options — A: confirm-once — a new method version must be confirmed by the trader in TD before its first payout; the registered 72-h cooldown guards changes; no per-payout re-confirmation; B: confirm every payout (strongest anti-fraud, but a step on every payout). See docs/62 §3.
design_questions.answer: **Answered 2026-09-20 — option A:** confirm-once at first payout + the 72-h cooldown. docs/11 §3 + api/pay.md written.

design_questions.question: CREDENTIAL DELIVERY (BRG-06): traders need their MT5 credentials, NOT-05 has no credentials template, and the email-vs-security question was carried twice (bridge pass, NOT pass). Options — A: ops-runbook delivery in V1 — staff copy credentials from the ADM detail view (sensitive-read audited, the KYC-doc pattern) and deliver through the firm's own channel; no template; automated V2 delivery with its own security design (one-time link); B: automated email in V1 (convenient, but live trading credentials in email). See docs/62 §3.
design_questions.raised_by: Twenty-first-pass sweep (docs/62; carried from docs/51 + docs/58)
design_questions.answer: **Answered 2026-09-20 — option A:** ops-runbook delivery in V1; no template (the D61 set stands). docs/08 §2/§16 + api/brg.md written.

design_questions.question: CHECKOUT CATALOG GAPS: CHK-02 reserves a coupon with no coupon model, TD-09 mentions add-ons with no catalog representation, and CHK-08/40 have no numbering scheme (three open TODOs since the thirteenth pass). Options — A: minimal V1 shapes — coupons as tenant-managed catalog rows (code, %/flat off, usage limit, expiry; challenge.write family; validated at reservation), add-ons defer to V2, ORD-/INV-{TENANT}-{YY}-{seq6} numbering; B: leave all three for the contract-freeze session with the tenant's finance input. See docs/62 §3.
design_questions.answer: **Answered 2026-09-20 — option A:** minimal V1 shapes for all three; docs/12 §9 + api/chk.md written.

design_questions.question: RELAY FAILOVER: the relay is exactly one instance (docs/01 §1.1: locked via PG advisory lock). What supervises it, how long is detection-to-restart, what happens to in-flight outbox rows, and what does a stalled relay do to notifications and tenant webhooks — or is this an accepted risk rather than a designed path? (Open since the 01 §1.1 'exactly one instance' note; the 04 §16 risk line only says 'outbox is durable + restart is the fix'.)
design_questions.answer: **Answered 2026-09-20 — designed path, not accepted risk (full story in docs/06 §3.7).** Supervisor = compose `restart: always` on the prod box (compose IS the process supervisor there; the D56 standby host is a disaster standby, not an active HA pair — there is no second relay to fail over to) + the `relay:lock` PG advisory lock with a 30 s heartbeat steal (docs/04 §3.3) — a second/started relay cannot publish while the lock is held, and a dead one is stolen within 30 s. Detection = `relay.lag` Prometheus metric + CON gauge (docs/04 §11) and the `evt.relay_stopped` CRITICAL after 60 s without a publish (docs/04 §6 ext) + Uptime Kuma on `/readyz` (readyz already gates on relay lag < 60 s, docs/04 §4). Worst-case detection-to-restart ≈ 60–90 s. In-flight: nothing is in flight — rows leave the outbox only after the XADD batch succeeds (`published_at IS NULL` is the work queue, docs/04 §3.3); a relay that dies mid-run leaves rows in PG to be drained on restart, and at-least-once redelivery is absorbed by consumer idempotency on `event_id`. Exit criterion: kill relay 5 min → restart → zero lost, zero dupes (docs/04 §16 step 2). Backlog impact: notifications (NOT), tenant webhooks (Hook0 via consumers), LED postings, and ANA read models lag by the stall duration + drain time; the **trading path is unaffected** (bridge enforcement does not depend on events, docs/04 §16 risks). V2 candidate (not V1 scope): dual-relay lease handover for <30 s failover.

design_questions.question: STREAM RUNTIME: MetaApi's real-time account data (broker equity on every price packet, positions, deals) is only practically reachable through its streaming API, which MetaApi says to consume via its SDK (JS/Python/Java — no Go SDK). The bridge is Go (docs/01 §2 rejected Node for the hot sync path). How should the platform host the streaming client: a Node/TS sidecar on the official SDK, a Go port of the socket.io protocol, or a Java SDK sidecar?
design_questions.raised_by: Twenty-second pass — BRG streaming ingestion (2026-09-25, docs/63)
design_questions.answer: **Answered 2026-09-25 — a thin Node/TS `bridge-stream` sidecar on the official `metaapi.cloud-sdk` (pinned 29.3.3).** The sidecar holds one SynchronizationListener per account and forwards ordered frames (Equity, AccountInfo, Positions, Deal, SyncState, Health, Downgrade) to the Go bridge over gRPC on a Unix socket. It does no money math (numbers cross as decimal strings; Go rounds per docs/09), holds no durable state (a PG-backed SDK HistoryStorage cursor lives in the bridge), makes no decisions, and reads equity only from raw packet values — never the SDK's local recompute (docs/63 F5). Recorded as ADR-15 (docs/01) — the one scoped exception to the Go-core rule. Rejected: a Go protocol port (we would own an evolving protocol MetaApi says not to re-implement); a Java sidecar (JVM on the single box + a third language). Licence = source-available, free for metaapi.cloud use → docs/34 review-before-deploy.

design_questions.question: INGEST MODE: docs/08 fixed V1 as poll-only every 60 s with streaming (BRG-21) in V3. MetaApi's documented CPU-credit limits (≈176 credits per account poll; 18k credits/min per front-end server) cap a 60-s poll at ≈100 accounts per server — V1's 431 accounts need ≥5 servers via client-id rotation, and V2's 10k accounts (≈1.76M credits/min) exceed all 12 servers combined (≈216k/min) ~8×; poll lag (≤60 s) is also enforcement lag. Streaming consumes no credits. Should V1 ingest move to streaming?
design_questions.raised_by: Twenty-second pass — BRG streaming ingestion (2026-09-25, docs/63)
design_questions.answer: **Answered 2026-09-25 — streaming is the V1 primary ingest; REST polling is demoted to fallback + reconciliation.** BRG-21 is pulled forward from V3 to V1 (workbook unchanged; recorded in docs/08 §1 and docs/99). Accounts whose stream is `stale` > 30 s are REST-polled every 60 s under a per-client-id credit budget (≤80% of the per-server limit; funded/open-position accounts first); REST also serves the D33 history-window check at every (re)synchronization + hourly, BRG-09 on-demand refresh when the stream is not live, commands, and the nightly reconciler. Provisioning sets reliability (high for funded), region per broker group, riskManagementApiEnabled=false, metastatsApiEnabled=false; G2 required. Rejected: V1 poll-only with streaming in V2 (still needs client-id sharding, keeps 60-s lag); keep V3.

design_questions.question: HOT PATH: per-quote equity (≈3k frames/s at 10k accounts, 10k/s bursts) cannot ride the outbox (relay capacity 10k events/min; every event is kept 13 months). How do streamed updates reach EVL with minimum latency without breaking ADR-6 (transactional outbox) — conflate at the bridge and keep the outbox, grant an ADR-6 exception for a tick stream, or call EVL directly with async persistence?
design_questions.raised_by: Twenty-second pass — BRG streaming ingestion (2026-09-25, docs/63)
design_questions.answer: **Answered 2026-09-25 — keep the transactional outbox; conflate at the bridge; group commit; NOTIFY doorbell.** The bridge holds per-account hot state and emits `bridge.tick` only on triggers: deal, position change (urgent), guard (equity within a guard band — default 50 bps of initial balance — of an EVL floor hint, ≤4/s; a floor crossing is never rate-capped, invariant I-21), material (abs Δequity ≥ 10 bps, ≤1/10 s), heartbeat (60 s open / 300 s flat, only while live), resync. A group-commit writer (≤25 ms / ≤500 rows; urgent = now) writes snapshots + deals + outbox + pg_notify('outbox_doorbell') in one tx; the relay LISTENs (1-s safety poll kept; NOTIFY is never transport). EVL returns advisory floor hints (evaluation_state.floor_daily/total/target + Redis `evl.floors`) — they change only when a tick is emitted, never what is decided. `bridge.tick` stays v1 with optional trigger/source/stream_seq/equity_low_cents/equity_high_cents (evidence; V1 rules still run at equity_cents). Envelope: V1 ≈10/s, V2 ≤250/s sustained, ≤1k/s burst (same order as the old poll plan); relay target raised to 60k events/min; platform-internal quote→verdict p95 < 50 ms. Correction: a relay stall pauses evaluation (docs/63 F6) — `bridge`-topic lag alert WARN 5 s / CRITICAL 30 s. Rejected: ADR-6 exception; direct bridge→EVL gRPC with async persistence.

design_questions.question: RISK-MANAGEMENT API: MetaApi's risk-management ('prop trading') API offers server-side drawdown/profit trackers with a resumable tracker-event stream, period statistics and equity charts. Should Alpha One use it — as a verdict source, as a watchdog, or not at all? (Tracker drawdown is measured against the period's initialBalance, has no trailing high-water mark, does not support MT5 netting, and is billed per account-hour on top of MetaApi; BVR-28 forbids vendor-final breaches.)
design_questions.raised_by: Twenty-second pass — BRG streaming ingestion (2026-09-25, docs/63)
design_questions.answer: **Answered 2026-09-25 — optional V2 watchdog, off by default; never a verdict source.** When a tenant/program opts in, BRG mirrors the rule pack into trackers (daily loss → period 'date', total loss → 'lifetime' absolute threshold; trailing-HWM programs and netting accounts get none) and long-polls /users/current/tracker-events/stream with a PG-persisted previousSequenceNumber cursor. A tracker event on a live stream with no EVL breach within 30 s → `bridge.watchdog_divergence` (ext) → ADM review; on a stale stream → immediate BRG-09 REST refresh → urgent tick → EVL decides. Never touches LCC (BVR-28). EquityBalanceListener (a duplicate streaming connection), equity charts (ANA owns) and MetaStats/CopyFactory are not on the ingest path. Cost passed through (docs/22 §3.4).

design_questions.section: EVL state ownership — the stateless engine re-confirmed (twenty-third pass — docs/64 §4.1)
design_questions.question: STATE OWNERSHIP: the binding architecture assigns `evaluation_state`, per-account ordering, idempotency, retry and DLQ to a Go `workers` consumer (docs/63 §4.1's topology, docs/04 §3.5 + §13, docs/09 §2/§3.2), and ADR-11 says the Rust engine is stateless. But `propfirm-engine` has grown a tenant-scoped Postgres `AccountStore` with optimistic concurrency (1,838 lines, 9 migrations, its own `accounts`/`positions`/`trades`/`events` schema), its own `IdempotencyStore`, its own rule-pack lifecycle and service-bearer auth, and `/internal/v1/{evaluate,override,manual-run,emergency-stop}` endpoints that read and write account state directly — `/evaluate` loads the account from its own store instead of taking state in the request. Two components now both believe they own account state, and it was never decided either way. Options — A: pare the engine back to ADR-11's scope (a stateless compute service) and build the `workers` consumer on docs/04 §3.5's existing pattern; B: keep the self-contained engine and delete the planned `workers` evaluation consumer; C: write a bespoke Rust consumer for the `evaluation` lane only; D: keep both and reconcile with OCC. Which, and why — before the multi-tenant scale-up, because two owners of account state is a much worse problem at 100k accounts across 10 tenants than at 431?
design_questions.raised_by: Twenty-third pass — EVL state ownership + the multi-tenant capacity correction (2026-09-25, docs/64)
design_questions.deadline: Before the multi-tenant scale-up — docs/64 §6 step 1 (the `workers` consumer) must land before the engine is stripped
design_questions.answer: **Answered 2026-09-25 — A. The Rust engine is pared back to ADR-11's original scope: a stateless compute service `evaluate(state, rules, tick) → (verdict, new_state, hints)`, with no database connection of its own, no tenant/account CRUD and no idempotency store. ADR-11 is re-confirmed and dated, not superseded.** State ownership, per-account/per-tenant ordering, retries and DLQ move to a `workers` evaluation consumer built on the platform's **existing** Go consumer-supervisor pattern (docs/04 §3.5: per-entity serial lanes via consistent hashing, `(event_id, consumer)` idempotency in `consumer_state`, `max_attempts: 5` with `1 s × 2^k`, `dlq.{consumer}` + the `relay dlq retry` path) — the same mechanism NOT/LED/AUD already use, not a new one invented for EVL. **Why, so this is not silently re-litigated:** (1) duplicating ordering/idempotency/retry semantics across two implementations is a maintenance *and correctness* liability that gets materially worse at white-label multi-tenant scale — every fix is made and tested twice and the two drift, as this review already found four times (an unconsulted `RulePackStore`, two idempotency semantics, a doc-comment contradicting its own function, generator drift); (2) a stateless compute tier is what makes horizontal scaling of the engine trivial — add replicas, no sharding logic of its own to get right — which matters directly at 100k+ accounts, whereas a stateful engine makes N replicas N competing writers on the same rows; (3) docs/09 §3.2's single-writer-per-account guarantee becomes **structural** rather than transactional, because OCC detects a violated invariant and the spec asks for one that cannot be violated. **Moves to `workers`:** the Postgres-backed `AccountStore` (reads/writes of `evaluation_state`), the idempotency store, per-account/tenant ordering, retry/DLQ, and the parts of `override`/`manual-run`/`emergency-stop` that mutate persisted account state (the *decision* of whether to allow an override stays engine logic; the *write* belongs in `workers`). **Stays in `propfirm-engine`:** the pure rule/decision math (`pure::evaluate`, everything under `rules/`, `engine/decision.rs`, `risk/`), the rule-pack schema/**validation** logic, the `EquityInput` provenance guard, the proptest + golden-replay corpus, and a narrow HTTP surface (`/evaluate`, plus new stateless `/rule-packs/validate` and `/explain`, plus the probes) — 14 routes reduced to 7, dispositioned case by case in docs/64 §4.3. Rule-pack **storage and lifecycle** (draft/active/superseded) move to where ADM's editor persists them, which resolves the long-standing 'RulePackStore isn't consulted during evaluation' gap **by removing the parallel-and-disconnected system rather than connecting it**. Rejected: B (contradicts docs/04 §3.5, docs/09 §2/§3.2 and docs/63 §4.1, forfeits the `consumer_state`/DLQ/replay tooling ops already uses, and leaves the engine owning a sharding problem at the scale where sharding mistakes are expensive); C (a *third* ordering/idempotency implementation, and it would put the money-loop lane outside `relay dlq …` and the CON DLQ screen); D (that is today's state, and findings G1–G4 are its output). **Blocker registered:** the `workers` evaluation consumer does not exist yet (`pf-platform/go/` has `gw/` and `bridge/` but no `workers/`), so the migration is consumer-first — stripping the engine before the consumer lands would leave the platform with no evaluation path at all (docs/64 §6). **Open item O-1, stated so it cannot hide behind a green build:** removing the disconnected store does *not* by itself make tenant-authored rule packs effective — `workers` must pass the bound `(rule_pack_id, version)` and `/evaluate` must build its registry from that document rather than the account's plan preset. Full text: docs/64.

design_questions.section: Per-tenant fairness on the event bus (twenty-third pass — docs/63 §4.13)
design_questions.question: TENANT FAIRNESS: at the corrected target (10 tenants × 10k accounts, docs/29 §1.1) nothing prevents one tenant's traffic spike from degrading another tenant's evaluation latency. Two mechanisms cause it: all tenants sharing one `topic.bridge` stream means one consumer group chews one FIFO (a tenant generating 80 % of ticks takes ≈ 80 % of consumer capacity), and `workers`' globally-hashed lanes mean a tenant's accounts share **serial** lanes with other tenants' accounts, so tenant A's backlog head-of-line-blocks tenant B's accounts on the same lane — invisible in aggregate throughput. Options — A: shard Redis Streams per tenant (separate stream keys, consumer groups per shard); B: shard per tenant-*tier*; C: per-tenant weighted fair queuing across `workers` lanes on a shared stream. Which?
design_questions.raised_by: Twenty-third pass — EVL state ownership + the multi-tenant capacity correction (2026-09-25, docs/64)
design_questions.answer: **Answered 2026-09-25 — A. One Redis Stream per tenant (`topic.bridge.{tenant_id}`) with its own consumer group, plus `workers` lane sets owned by exactly one tenant shard.** Lane allocation is weighted with a floor: `max(10, ceil(weight_t × total))` per tenant, total `max(128, 10 × tenants)`, `weight_t` defaulting to the tenant's share of deployed accounts and CON-editable. **The floor of 10 lanes is that tenant's own burst design point** (10 lanes × ≈ 100 ticks/s = 1,000 ticks/s = docs/63 §4.4's per-tenant burst), so a tenant can absorb its own news burst without borrowing capacity it may not get back. The supervisor round-robins over tenant lane sets that have work; within a set, lanes stay serial per account (`hash(account_id) → lane`, docs/04 §3.5 unchanged). **Why sharding and not C (weighted fair queuing on a shared stream): C is not implementable on Redis Streams without sharding.** `XREADGROUP >` delivers undelivered entries in stream-id order to whichever consumer asks, so the consumer never chooses which tenant's work to take next — the stream decides. Exercising a choice requires either per-tenant streams or reading into a local buffer and reordering there, which abandons ADR-7's at-least-once-plus-idempotent simplicity and adds unbounded in-process buffering to a component whose job is to be restartable. Per-tenant streams are the *precondition* for any fairness policy; WFQ is then trivially expressible on top, which is what the lane weights implement. **B (tenant-tier) rejected** because it re-creates mechanism 1 inside a tier. One stream per tenant (rather than per tier) is affordable — 10 streams × `MAXLEN ~100k` × ≈ 1 KB ≈ 1 GB, inside `redis-streams`' 2 GB (D51); ≈ 5 GB at docs/00 §5's 50 tenants, so the D51 2/2/4 split becomes 2/6/4 — and it aligns the isolation unit with everything else already per tenant: docs/63 §4.2's shard ownership (the hash becomes `(tenant_id, account_id)`, 5 shards per tenant), §4.7's MetaApi credential set and credit budget, and docs/00 §8 #2. **One tenant = one shard set = one stream = one lane set = one credit budget.** The section also fixes the `MAXLEN ~100000` **trim hazard** the sharding exposes: a 5-minute fleet-wide burst puts ≈ 150k entries behind one tenant's group, past the trim point. Trimmed entries are not lost (the outbox + `events` log are the replay source, ADR-6/7) but silent trimming would be a silent evaluation gap, so the consumer compares `last-delivered-id` against `XINFO STREAM`'s `first-entry`/`max-deleted-entry-id`, emits **`evl.stream_trimmed`** and replays that tenant's range from PG; D84's shedding is the prevention. `MAXLEN` is deliberately **not** raised to ~1M (≈ 10 GB at 10 tenants) because Redis is never the source of truth (docs/00 §8 #1). DLQ stays single per consumer with `tenant_id` in the envelope and a per-tenant depth alert. Accepted by load test **LT-4/I-31**: with tenant A at 10× weight, tenants B–J's quote→verdict p95 is unchanged within measurement noise and no `evl.tick_stale` fires outside A. Full text: docs/63 §4.13.

design_questions.section: Postgres write scaling for `evaluation_state` at the corrected target (twenty-third pass — docs/29 §3.4)
design_questions.question: PG WRITE SCALING: at 100,000 accounts the evaluation path is ≈ 11.8k q/s sustained and ≈ 42.9k q/s burst (≈ 2.6k / ≈ 10.1k commits/s) against a single AX42-class primary planned at ≈ 10k q/s. A 5-minute burst at 10k ticks/s against a 5k ticks/s write path drains in exactly **10 minutes = the `evl.tick_stale` threshold**, i.e. zero margin against the correctness backstop. Options — A: partition by `tenant_id` and stay single-primary; B: adopt horizontal Postgres (Citus) now; C: shard by `account_id`; D: a second primary with per-tenant write routing; E: do nothing and rely on `evl.tick_stale`. Also: what is the read-replica story for ANA, disputes and ADM, and is single-primary-with-partitioning sufficient at this target or must the plan include a horizontal option?
design_questions.raised_by: Twenty-third pass — EVL state ownership + the multi-tenant capacity correction (2026-09-25, docs/64)
design_questions.deadline: Before the V2 second box is bought — the trigger is measured (docs/29 §1.1.1 trigger 6, load test LT-5)
design_questions.answer: **Answered 2026-09-25 — A, with the horizontal option staged on a measured trigger rather than adopted or dismissed.** (1) **Partition `evaluation_state` by `tenant_id`** (hash, 64 buckets — covers docs/00 §5's 50-tenant range without re-partitioning, and a power of two so D82's shard mapping and the bucket mapping agree); every evaluation query is tenant-scoped by docs/00 §8 #2, so pruning applies to 100 % of the hot path. (2) **Partition `account_snapshots` and `broker_deals` by `(tenant_id, day)`** — their write volume *is* comparable (1,667/s and 58/s vs 2,500/s) and their row counts are far larger (≈ 2.0 B and ≈ 450 M in their rolling windows), so day partitioning turns retention into `DROP PARTITION` instead of a `DELETE` over billions of rows. (3) **Partition `events` by day** and give `bridge.tick` a **≤ 7-day hot window + R2 columnar archive** (docs/63 F13: 13 months (≈ 395 d) at 2,500/s is ≈ 85 B rows ≈ 34 TB vs docs/29 §1.3's '≈ 200 GB/yr, 1 TB disk' — ≈ 605 GB hot and ≈ 3 TB/yr ≈ $45/mo archived instead). Every other topic keeps the 13-month PG window; they are 3–4 orders of magnitude smaller. (4) **One write path per account, structurally** — D81 + D82 together are what make docs/09 §3.2's single-writer guarantee real; before D81 the engine's OCC `AccountStore` was a second writer and OCC turned a correctness property into a retry loop. **Read-replica story: nothing outside the evaluation write path reads the primary.** `workers` (the lane's state read+write), the bridge's floor-hint reload on cache miss, and PAY eligibility (BRG-09 — a payout decision must not read a lagging replica) stay on the primary; ANA's read model, dispute replay, ADM/TD screens and RSK's batch detectors read the replica under the `_ro` role, and dispute replay older than the F13 hot window reads the R2 archive rather than PG at all. Replication is physical streaming (docs/06 §3.3's failover strategy extended, doing double duty as the read scale-out and the D56 warm-standby promotion path), lag WARN 10 s / CRITICAL 60 s, and every human-visible replica read carries `as_of` so lag is disclosed (ANA-14). The replica lives on box 2, which is a **V2 prerequisite** (docs/63 F12) and carries `bridge-stream` shards *and* the replica — complementary loads (RSS-heavy + read-heavy) rather than two writers. **Is single-primary-with-partitioning sufficient? Sustained: yes** (≈ 11.8k q/s, ≈ 2.6k commits/s against a ≈ 10k-commit/s NVMe ceiling ⇒ ~4× commit headroom, ~1.2× CPU headroom). **Burst: no** — but burst need not be served at line rate, only drained inside the staleness window, and the drain arithmetic lands at exactly 10 minutes = the `evl.tick_stale` threshold, i.e. **zero margin**. That is why D84's shedding ladder exists (it removes ≈ 14 % of sustained load at level 1, ≈ 30 % at level 2 and ≈ 60 % at level 3, for zero correctness cost at levels 1–2, because it widens the conflation window rather than dropping observations — `equity_low/high_cents` still bound the gap, I-22) and why the horizontal option is staged rather than dismissed: **adopt Citus (distribution key `tenant_id`) when the load test or production shows sustained commits > 6,000/s (60 % of the ceiling, docs/29 §1.2's 2× rule applied to commits) for 2 weeks, or `evl_lag_seconds > 300` more than twice a month with the engine tier demonstrably unsaturated.** Not adopted now because the sustained load does not require it, because shedding is ~200 lines in a component that already exists while Citus is a new database topology, because Citus conflicts with docs/00 §8 #6 (operable by a 1-person DevOps team), and because ADR-6's outbox is a single-database transaction that would become a distributed one (solvable by co-locating a tenant's outbox with its evaluation rows under the same distribution key, but it must be designed, not discovered during an incident). **Partitioning first is not a dead end: `tenant_id` hash partitioning and a Citus `tenant_id` distribution key are the same sharding function, so the migration is a shard move, not a data-model change.** Rejected: C (sharding by `account_id` breaks tenant locality and docs/00 §8 #2); D (two write paths turn the single-writer guarantee into a coordination problem); E (`evl.tick_stale` is a correctness backstop, not a capacity plan — reaching it on funded accounts is already a docs/29 §4 SLO failure). **All throughput figures are planning estimates derived from documented per-unit limits, not measurements**; load test LT-5 retires them. Full text and the per-writer table: docs/29 §3.4.

design_questions.section: Autoscaling signal and load-shedding for the stateless engine tier (twenty-third pass — docs/63 §4.14)
design_questions.question: CAPACITY CONTROL: once D81 makes the engine genuinely stateless, what is the autoscaling signal, and what happens when lag outpaces scaling? `evl.tick_stale` (implemented, 10-minute threshold) stops verdicts on stale equity and is the correctness backstop — but it is not a capacity plan. What lag threshold pages someone, what is allowed to degrade gracefully, and what counts as an incident? Note the deployment target is Docker Compose on Hetzner (ADR-9) with no Kubernetes (docs/00 §8 #6), so there is no autoscaler to wire a metric to.
design_questions.raised_by: Twenty-third pass — EVL state ownership + the multi-tenant capacity correction (2026-09-25, docs/64)
design_questions.deadline: With the `workers` evaluation consumer (docs/64 §6 step 5); thresholds confirmed by load test LT-6
design_questions.answer: **Answered 2026-09-25 — Redis Streams consumer-group lag expressed as *time-to-drain*, acted on by an operator in V2, with load-shedding that widens the conflation window rather than dropping observations.** **The honest constraint first: the deployment target has no autoscaler.** ADR-9 is Compose on one Hetzner box and docs/00 §8 #6 forbids Kubernetes; Compose has `--scale` but no controller. So the story is stated for the platform that exists: in **V2** the signal is scraped by Prometheus and acted on by an **operator** (`docker compose up -d --scale engine=N --scale workers=M`, a runbook line, surfaced in CON); in **V2.5** — *only if the load test proves the manual loop too slow* — a ~200-line Compose-scale actuator reads the same metric within min/max bounds (explicitly optional, explicitly a new deployable, justified by measured operator response time before it is built); in **V3** the same metric feeds KEDA/HPA, which is why it is defined in lag terms rather than CPU. **The signal is lag in seconds, not entries**, because that is the quantity comparable to the correctness backstop: `evl_lag_seconds{tenant,group} = lag_entries ÷ measured_drain_rate`, `lag_entries` from `XINFO GROUPS → lag` (Redis ≥ 7.0), `measured_drain_rate` an EWMA of acknowledged entries/s over 60 s per group. Supporting metrics: `evl_stream_lag_entries`, `evl_lane_queue_depth{tenant,lane}`, `evl_evaluate_seconds` (the engine HTTP call — the stateless tier's own saturation), `evl_pg_state_seconds` (the shared resource), `evl_shed_level{tenant}`, `evl_stream_trimmed_total{tenant}`. **Engine CPU is deliberately not the scaling signal:** `propfirm-engine`'s `benches/engine.rs` measures ≈ 52,600 pure evals/s single-threaded (≈ 205k/s batched), so at a 10k verdict/s target the engine is never the bottleneck — HTTP fan-in and Postgres are, and scaling on engine CPU would add replicas to a tier that is not saturated while the real constraint goes unaddressed. **Thresholds are fractions of the 10-minute `evl.tick_stale` window (docs/09 §6), not chosen arbitrarily:** scale out at > 60 s for 60 s; **WARN** at > 120 s for 5 min (⇒ shed level 1, no page); **PAGE (P1) at > 300 s for 60 s** — half the window, i.e. verdicts begin being suppressed in ≈ 5 min if nothing changes; **INCIDENT** at > 480 s, or on any `evl.stream_trimmed`, or on any `evl.tick_stale` suppression on a **funded** account — declared, tenant-visible via CON-15, with the docs/29 §4 breach-to-enforcement SLO *formally suspended* for the duration and the suspension recorded; scale in below 30 s for 10 min. **What degrades gracefully: shedding raises the bridge conflator's thresholds — the same mechanism D79 already uses, not a new one — so a shed tick is not a lost observation, because `equity_low_cents`/`equity_high_cents` keep bounding what happened between emitted ticks (invariant I-22).** Level 1 (`heartbeat` 60 s → 180 s open / 300 s → 900 s flat, **non-funded accounts only**) takes the non-funded heartbeat term from 367/s to 122/s = **≈ 14 % of the ≈ 1,791/s sustained fleet rate, for zero correctness cost**; level 2 (+ `material` 10 bps → 25 bps for non-funded) is cumulative **≈ 30 %**; level 3 (+ funded heartbeats widen too **except guard-band accounts**, `material` widened fleet-wide, non-funded lane weight to the floor) is cumulative **≈ 60 %** — the ceiling is ≈ 60 % and not 100 % because funded accounts are half the fleet and the priority list protects them. Levels 1–2 cost nothing because heartbeats carry no new information (they only bound the stale-floor-hint worst case, ≤ 60 s → ≤ 180 s for non-funded) and **widening the interval cannot trip `evl.tick_stale`**, which measures tick *age* — `now − occurred_at`, the receive time of the newest frame folded in, including the `Health` frames arriving at ≤ 1 per 10 s while `live` — not emission cadence; a heartbeat never refreshes stale data and a `stale` stream emits none at all (docs/09 §6). Level 2 adds `material` 10 bps → 25 bps for non-funded accounts. Level 3 (the incident level) drops non-funded challenge accounts' lane weight to the floor while funded and guard-band accounts keep full rate. **The ordering reuses docs/63 §4.7's existing resync priority list (guard-band → funded → open positions → the rest) rather than inventing a new one.** **Never shed:** `deal`, `position`, `guard`, `guard`-crossing (I-21 — a crossing quote is never conflated away) and `resync` — the triggers that can change a verdict. **Delivery reuses the `evl.floors` pattern:** `workers` publishes `evl.load_shed {tenant_id, level, reason, at}` on Redis pub/sub and the bridge applies it, so the decision is made where lag is observable and the act happens where the tick is born (no outbox row, relay `XADD` or PG write is spent on a tick about to be deferred); Redis-down degrades to level 0 at the bridge — the safe direction — with the same 30 s PG-reload fallback floor hints use. **`evl.tick_stale` is explicitly not a capacity plan:** a system that reaches it on funded accounts has already failed its docs/29 §4 SLO, which is why that condition is an incident and not a degradation. Accepted by load tests **LT-6/I-30** (the ladder removes ≈ 14 % / ≈ 30 % / ≈ 60 % at levels 1/2/3 as predicted; zero `deal`/`position`/`guard`/crossing/`resync` ticks shed at any level; I-22 holds across every widened window) and LT-7 (the trim hazard). Full text: docs/63 §4.14.

triage.source: scripts/prd-workbook.json (docs/37 open rows), triaged in the 2026-09-20 gap-closure pass
triage.note: Every docs/37 open PRD question is assigned to the stakeholder who can answer it. Rows in the internal bucket carry a proposed answer marked 'Proposed — pending sign-off'; proposals adopt the PRD's own 'Recommended:' text where present, or the binding spec where it already decided the point. NO row is marked answered — sign-off is the owner's to give (the D-number convention: an answer lands only with a real owner decision).

rows.q: What trigger moves us from Compose to Kubernetes: service count, tenant count, or multi-region? Recommended: none of these in year one.
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: adopt 'none of these in year one'. docs/06 §11 keeps K8s forbidden, revisited only at > 50 tenants or multi-region.

rows.q: Backup retention period and off-host copy destination, for example a Hetzner Storage Box?
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: the 3-2-1 scheme is already binding (D55, docs/06 §2.4) — prod box + standby host + off-provider object store (B2/Wasabi, object lock, separate credentials); retention is tool-managed by pgBackRest, exact day-counts fixed at the freeze session.

rows.q: On-call rotation and alert channel for a 4 to 5 person team: which Telegram group or phone tree?
rows.note: Staffing decision: who is paged. The alert *set* is already defined (docs/06 §2.7/D76: CRITICAL pages), the roster is not.

rows.q: Staging data: synthetic only, or anonymized production copies, and what are the anonymization rules?
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: synthetic only — no production PII ever lands in staging (docs/28 PII posture; consistent with the companion row 'synthetic-only approved').

rows.q: Do we need a bastion or VPN for production access in V1, or is keyed SSH with fail2ban sufficient?
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: keyed SSH + UFW + fail2ban + Cloudflare origin-auth in V1 (docs/28 §3.1); bastion is a V2 item.

rows.q: What RPO and RTO does the business accept, for example RPO 15 minutes and RTO 4 hours?
rows.note: Business-acceptance question. The spec has already committed to RPO ≤ 5 min (pgBackRest, D55) and RTO ≤ 15 min promoted / ≤ 2 h worst case (D56, docs/06 §2.4) — COO confirms the business accepts those numbers; rejecting them overturns D55/D56, it is not a retune.

rows.q: PgBouncer in front of Postgres or application-level pooling only? Recommended: PgBouncer.
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: PgBouncer — already a V1 deployable (`db-proxy`, docs/01 §1.1).

rows.q: V1 database strategy: single instance with rehearsed restore inside RTO, or warm standby from day one? Recommended: single instance plus drills.
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: as documented post-D56 — prod single box (accepted SPOF, ADR-9/10) PLUS the D56 warm standby (disaster replica, promote ≤ 15 min, docs/06 §2.4/§11). The PRD's 'single plus drills' predates D55/D56 and is superseded by them.

rows.q: What are the load test target numbers: concurrent trader sessions, sync batch size, payout burst volume?

rows.q: Is synthetic-only staging data approved, meaning no production PII ever lands in staging? Recommended: yes.

rows.q: MetaApi or Brokeree for MT5? Decision criteria: provisioning API coverage, price per account, sandbox quality, support response.

rows.q: Does the broker contract grant API rights for account creation, disable, enable, close all, group assignment, and password reset, or are some manual in broker manager? If manual, enforcement and provisioning designs degrade.

rows.q: What is the default sync interval per tenant and the minimum safe interval given vendor rate limits?
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: per-account `poll_interval_s` default 60 (docs/32 `broker_accounts.poll_interval_s`); the interval widens ×2 automatically when p95 > 2 s and MetaApi rate limits are the binding constraint (docs/08 §3/§11).

rows.q: Daily drawdown reset follows broker server time or a tenant-configured timezone?
rows.note: Risk semantics — the reset instant defines 'daily drawdown'. (Same question raised under Evaluation Engine.)

rows.q: Which MT5 groups map to which phases, and who creates those groups at the broker, broker ops or API?
rows.note: Broker-side topology + who operates it.

rows.q: Do we store trader terminal passwords in our database or delegate password generation and delivery to the vendor? Needs a security review.
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: store platform-side, field-encrypted AES-256-GCM with key versioning (BRG-44; docs/32 `broker_accounts.credentials_enc`/`cred_key_version`). The security review at freeze verifies key handling — the storage decision itself is already made in the DDL.

rows.q: If the broker does not offer MatchTrader, is cTrader the fallback second platform for V1?
rows.note: Depends on broker platform support; the platform is MetaTrader 5 in V1 (docs/00/01).

rows.q: Can broker groups be created by API, or does broker ops create them manually per request?
rows.note: Broker capability — same family as the API-rights row; 'manual' means a human step in provisioning.

rows.q: Default sync interval per account phase: same interval for evaluation and funded, or faster for funded?

rows.q: Investor password: delivered by default in the credential email or only on request?
rows.note: Credential-delivery policy (same family as the lifecycle 'delivery channels' row).

rows.q: Enforcement retry policy: max attempts, backoff ceiling, and escalation SLA for ops response.
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: as designed in docs/08 — commands run `pending → executing → confirmed | failed(retry) → dead`; reconnect retries 3 with 30 s halving backoff; a dead enforcement command never auto-retries past dead → CON CRITICAL + human (the escalation SLA is the on-call response time in the docs/06 runbooks).

rows.q: At what active account count does MetaApi per- account pricing become more expensive than Brokeree or self-hosted alternatives?
rows.note: Vendor pricing data — a commercial input for the year-2 vendor review, not a V1 design input.

rows.q: Maximum tolerable sync outage before we alert traders or pause provisioning?
rows.note: Risk tolerance question (raised with the Risk Owner in the PRD).

rows.q: Does FunderBlu's Veriff contract include webhook endpoints or only polling? This affects KYC-05 implementation.
rows.note: Contract fact only Veriff can confirm; the platform handles both (webhook + poll fallback, docs/13).

rows.q: What KYC verification level does each FunderBlu challenge type require at migration? Map each challenge to basic, enhanced, or skipped.
rows.note: Compliance-level mapping per product — determines KYC-07/08 gates at cutover.

rows.q: Do we require proof of address in V1 or only ID plus liveness as Veriff defaults?
rows.note: KYC policy (jurisdiction-driven).

rows.q: What is the restricted country list for V1, and does it apply at registration, at KYC, or both?

rows.q: Which role can approve KYC manually in the fallback path, and does it require dual control?

rows.q: How many resubmission attempts are allowed before final rejection?
rows.note: KYC policy (same family as the 'before contact support' row).

rows.q: Do we store only Veriff media references, or also cache documents in our object storage for manual cases? Recommended: manual cases only.
rows.note: Data-retention choice. PRD recommends 'manual cases only' — consistent with the docs/13 §5 R2 retention posture; sign-off needed.

rows.q: What is the KYC document retention period required by FunderBlu's jurisdiction? This determines KYC-31 configuration.
rows.note: Jurisdiction retention law.

rows.q: Does FunderBlu require proof of address for all challenges or only funded accounts? This affects KYC- 28 configuration.
rows.note: KYC policy (funded = higher level is the usual answer; Legal confirms).

rows.q: What is the acceptable SLA for manual KYC review? Current target is 4 hours but confirm with operations.
rows.note: Staffing/SLA confirmation — the 4 h target is theirs to confirm.

rows.q: Do we need KYC re-verification on an annual cycle or only on document expiry?
rows.note: Compliance cycle (V2 machinery, KYC-21/25 — the answer sets scope).

rows.q: What happens to KYC data when a trader account is terminated? Immediate deletion, retention period, or anonymization?
rows.note: PII end-of-life policy.

rows.note: KYC level policy (Veriff configuration follows).

rows.q: Do we need to support KYC for traders who registered before the KYC module was live (migration backfill)?

rows.q: Confirm the exact V1 report list against the reports FunderBlu uses today in TTS: which of the eleven risk tabs map into V1?

rows.q: What timezone defines the daily and monthly cutoff for aggregates: tenant timezone or UTC?

rows.q: What is the read model rebuild procedure if a read model corrupts: full replay from the event log, and how long must that take?

rows.q: Which roles receive financial reports by default, and does the support role see any analytics at all?

rows.q: Which of TTS's report tabs must be reproduced at cutover, and which can wait? This gates cutover.

rows.note: Business definitions — the spec can only compute what the business defines.

rows.q: Is reporting day boundary in tenant timezone or UTC?
rows.note: Twin of the 'cutoff timezone' row — one answer.

rows.note: Freshness expectation per report (V1 default: nightly batch; near-real-time list = scope addition).

rows.q: How far back must trend data be retained for trend views?
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: 13 months — matches the event log retention the read models replay from (docs/19: 'retention 13 months (matches the events log, 04)'. Longer trends need the R2 archive, a V2 item).

rows.q: Does FunderBlu want the support inbox in the first cutover, or can Telegram/email remain primary until Phase 4?

rows.q: What are the V1 support categories: account, payout, KYC, payment, breach, technical, general, or a different list?

rows.q: What file types and size limits are allowed for attachments? Recommended: images and PDFs only, max 10 MB per file.

rows.q: Does Telegram intake mean full two-way sync in V1, or only linking Telegram messages manually to a ticket? Recommended: defer full sync.

rows.q: Should support staff be allowed to see payout destination details inside tickets, or should these remain masked unless the staff role has finance permission?

rows.q: Do resolved tickets auto-close after a fixed period, and what is the default duration?

rows.q: Daily drawdown reset follows broker server midnight or a tenant-configured reset time?
rows.note: Risk semantics — the reset instant defines 'daily drawdown' (same question as the Bridge row; one answer for both).

rows.q: What is the default basis, equity or balance, for daily and max drawdown across FunderBlu products?
rows.note: Risk semantics per product — drives the rule-pack defaults.

rows.q: Which rules are hard breach versus soft breach by default in V1 product configs?

rows.q: Does auto-pass apply to the final evaluation phase or does live verification always require manual review, as TTS defaulted?

rows.q: Which challenges get free retakes, how many, and is that configured per challenge or per tenant?

rows.q: How long do terminal accounts stay hot before archive, for example 12 months?

rows.q: Which TTS account states map to which new states, and do imported accounts keep original rule versions or bind to new versions?

rows.note: Commercial policy — non-commercial accounts and the payout gate.

rows.q: Which providers are confirmed for V1 launch: Match2Pay, Interkasa, and which crypto rail exactly?

rows.note: Money-control policy (the refund state machine exists, docs/12 §3.4; the window + role are the policy).

rows.q: How many network confirmations for crypto payments before provisioning starts?

rows.q: What is the second approval threshold amount for V1?
rows.note: Money-control threshold.

rows.q: Who designs and provides the HTML/CSS for the 10 core email templates?

rows.note: Strategic build-trigger (the module is V2 — docs/01 phase 3; the trigger decides WHEN).

rows.q: First iteration scope: templates plus pricing widget only, or include blog from the start? Recommended: templates and widget only.
rows.note: Scope call. PRD recommends templates + widget only.

rows.q: Does a hosted tenant site replace the tenant's existing website or coexist with it, for example platform hosts landing and pricing while the tenant keeps an external blog?
rows.note: Product model (coexist is the likely answer — it changes little engineering).

rows.q: Hosting model on our stack: Nginx vhosts per tenant on Hetzner, or edge-rendered static pages?
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: Nginx vhosts on the same Hetzner stack — boring, in line with docs/06; the CMS module is V2, so the decision can land with that phase.

rows.q: Is published content subject to an approval workflow in regulated markets, and who approves?
rows.note: Regulatory content-approval question.

rows.q: Do we offer import from WordPress or Webflow for existing tenant content, or start fresh only?
rows.note: Scope call (import = a V2+ engineering investment).

rows.q: What is the build trigger: named tenant demand or a marketing-led campaign plan? FunderBlu's previous competition module had zero conversions, so validate demand before spending effort.
rows.note: Strategic build-trigger — the zero-conversion history is the case for demand validation first.

rows.q: Do competition accounts use a separate demo group at the broker or reuse evaluation accounts, and does the broker support the needed group?
rows.note: Broker capability question (group support) + the mapping decision.

rows.q: Which scoring criteria ship in the first iteration: profit percent only, or also ROI and risk-adjusted score?
rows.note: Product scope (the scoring engine is agnostic — docs/24).

rows.q: Which prize types launch first: account credit, coupon, or cash payout, and which budget funds the prize pool?
rows.note: Budget + prize policy (cash prizes = payout-engine coupling).

rows.q: Is the leaderboard alias-only by default with opt-in real names, and what does legal say about public performance data?
rows.note: Public-performance-data question — Legal owns it (alias-only is the safe default).

rows.q: What leaderboard update frequency is acceptable at launch: batch per sync cycle or near real-time? Recommended: batch per sync.
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: batch per sync cycle — the docs/24 design reads the same ANA read models; near-real-time would be a separate stream consumer.

rows.q: Do competition results and badges become part of the trader's permanent record and certificates?
rows.note: Product/brand decision (touches the D61 closed certificate set).

rows.q: Confirm the pricing model: fixed plan plus usage overage, pure module-based pricing, or hybrid? This is a commercial decision, not an engineering one.
rows.note: Commercial decision — the question says it is not an engineering one.

rows.q: Which metering counters are billable: active traders, trading accounts, orders, API calls, or a subset?
rows.note: Pricing mechanics — pairs with the pricing-model row.

rows.q: Billing currency and tax handling per tenant jurisdiction: who validates the rules, and do invoices need reverse- charge wording for EU tenants?
rows.note: Tax compliance (reverse-charge wording is a Legal/finance question).

rows.q: Dunning policy: grace period length, and does past due mean suspension or read-only mode first?
rows.note: Collections policy (the suspension machinery is spec'd, TEN-15; the grace/first-step is policy).

rows.q: Is FunderBlu itself a billed subscription or exempt as the owner tenant, and how is that represented?
rows.note: Commercial self-dealing question.

rows.q: Do B2B collections reuse the trader payment adapters or a separate invoicing provider such as Stripe Billing?
rows.note: Vendor choice for B2B invoicing (no Stripe in V1 for trader rails, docs/12 — B2B is a separate question).

rows.q: Contract terms at launch: monthly only, or annual with discount?
rows.note: Commercial terms.

rows.q: Which languages get official SDKs at launch: TypeScript and Python only, or more?
rows.note: Scope call (V2 module — docs/01 phase 3; the launch set is product's to size).

rows.q: Sandbox data policy: synthetic data only, or masked production-shaped data? Recommended: synthetic only.
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: synthetic only — docs/28 PII posture (no production data in sandbox; the SDK-06 sandbox injects synthetic events).

rows.q: Is the developer portal a separate documentation site or a section of the platform marketing site?
rows.note: Product decision (docs hosting is the CMS/docs surface).

rows.q: Which BYO paths get documented first based on real demand: checkout, affiliate, or KYC?
rows.note: Demand signal — Sales owns it (unassigned role; the question was raised by 'Sales owner (unassigned)').

rows.q: Is public API access included in base plans or reserved for enterprise tiers? Ties into tenant billing.
rows.note: Commercial tiering decision.

rows.q: What is the support model for integrators: docs and sandbox only, or paid onboarding as professional services?
rows.note: Professional-services commercial decision.

rows.q: How many days of webhook delivery history is replayable in sandbox and in production?
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: production replay from the 13-month event log (docs/04) — practical V1 window 7 days (the outbox trim horizon); sandbox 30 days of synthetic events. Proposed defaults, tunable at the V2 API freeze.

rows.q: Is the developer portal public before we have external tenants? Recommended: private beta docs for design partners, public at the second tenant.
rows.note: Demand/timing call (raised with 'Sales owner (unassigned)').

rows.q: Do we monetize API access separately from plans with per-call pricing, or include quotas in tiers only? Ties into tenant billing.
rows.note: Commercial decision.

rows.q: Which API products ship first: read-only reports, webhooks, or account management?
rows.note: Demand signal — what design partners actually need.

rows.q: Does partner-delegated access ship in the first iteration, or do we start with tenant-owned keys only?
rows.note: Scope call (tenant-owned keys is the simple start).

rows.q: Is GraphQL real demand or speculation? Recommended: defer until two tenants explicitly request it.
rows.note: Demand validation. PRD recommends deferral until two tenants request it.

rows.q: Who owns portal content, guides, and tutorials, and what keeps them current across releases?
rows.note: Content ownership.

rows.q: Status page: build a minimal internal one or use an external provider such as Instatus? Recommended: external provider at launch.
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: external provider (Instatus) at launch — ops default, fits the docs/06 D57 monitoring stack (Uptime Kuma feeds it).

rows.q: Is 2FA mandatory for all staff roles in V1, or only finance and risk roles?
rows.note: Staff security policy (the spec already forces MFA on the platform org, docs/02/06 — the per-role breadth is Ops' call).

rows.q: Do we ship Google OAuth in V1 or defer all social login?
rows.note: Scope call (ZITADEL supports it, ADR-13 — shipping it is a config + support-surface decision).

rows.q: What are the access token and refresh token lifetimes and rotation rules?
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: 15-min access token (binding — docs/02/43: the 15-min access token bounds IdP-sync exposure); session expiry idle > 30 min / absolute 24 h (docs/02 §5); refresh rotation with reuse detection (`auth.session_revoked`, docs/02).

rows.q: Do migrated TTS traders get a forced password reset at cutover or a reset-email flow?
rows.note: Cutover procedure decision (migration runbook, docs/25).

rows.q: Does any V1 tenant require SSO or SAML, which would pull it into V1 scope?
rows.note: Commercial fact — 'does any V1 tenant require X' is a sales/COO fact, not an engineering guess (ZITADEL ships SSO/SAML, ADR-13 — enabling it is a config + SCIM scope question).

rows.q: Do we allow super admin impersonation of tenant admins for support, and under what audit rules?
rows.note: Access policy (the view-as machinery + deny-list exist, docs/21; the allow + audit rules are Ops').

rows.q: Do outbound tenant webhooks ship in V1 or immediately after MVP , given FunderBlu does not need them?
rows.note: Scope call. Note: the platform SHIPS Hook0 in V1 (docs/01 §1.1 deployable; EVT-10/signed delivery) — the question is whether FunderBlu *uses* it at launch; the build-vs-use distinction is CEO's.

rows.q: Redis Streams retention: what max stream length and retention window do we configure for V1?
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: per the docs/04 §11 parameters — MAXLEN ~100k per stream (approximate trim, keeps XADD O(1)); streams are transport only, rebuildable from the 13-month `events` log (docs/04 §5.4).

rows.q: Event log retention period for replay: 90 days, 1 year, or permanent archive to object storage?
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: 13 months in PG, then archive to R2 — already binding (docs/04: 'retention: V1 keep 13 months, then archive to R2 (EVT-22)').

rows.q: Who approves event schema changes and version bumps to prevent contract drift between modules?
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: module owner proposes, contract gates enforce — ADR-7 additive-only versioning (bump `version` on payload change; unknown-higher → DLQ + alert), enforced by the docs/99 0.10 contract checks (catalog + schema + payload gates). A schema change is a PR against `contracts/` reviewed by the module owner + BE lead.

rows.q: Is the outbox relay a separate process or a background worker inside the API binary for V1? Recommended: separate process.
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: separate process — binding (docs/01 §1.1 `relay` deployable; the failover story is docs/06 §3.7 / D76).

rows.q: Do any V1 flows require stronger than at-least-once delivery plus idempotent consumers? Expected answer is no.
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: none — at-least-once + idempotent consumers IS the binding semantics (ADR-6/7, docs/04 §4.3); no V1 flow needs exactly-once at the bus level (money paths are guarded by idempotency keys + state machines instead).

rows.q: What are the default rate limits per route group for trader, admin, and webhook traffic?
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: the binding table (docs/55 §4.6) — per-user 100 rpm (tenant-plan adjustable), auth 10 / 5 min, payout 5 / h, Cloudflare per-IP edge limit outside; inbound provider webhooks are handler-deduped by provider event id (no app rate limit).

rows.q: Do per-tenant quotas ship in V1 or only after the second paying tenant? Expected: after.
rows.note: Commercial trigger (the quota machinery GW-29 exists; WHEN it ships is a business call).

rows.q: Versioning strategy: URL versioning only, or also header-based negotiation? Recommended: URL only.
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: URL only — the spec is built on /v1/... with Deprecation/Sunset headers (docs/55 GW-28; docs/04 §4.2 envelope).

rows.q: Do we expose a public tenant API in V1 or only inbound and outbound webhooks? Ties to the EVT-11 question.
rows.note: Scope call. Spec posture: the public tenant API is V2 (docs/01 phase 3; EVT-11) — V1 = inbound provider webhooks + outbound tenant webhooks only.

rows.q: Who defines and reviews the PII exclusion list for request logs?
rows.note: PII policy (the redaction machinery exists, docs/04/28; the list is Legal's).

rows.q: Custom domain SSL in V1: manual via Cloudflare for SaaS, or automated certificate provisioning?
rows.note: Proposed — pending sign-off: V1 is subdomain-only ({slug}.alpha1.io, docs/03); custom domain is the V1.1 provisioning step (docs/03 §3 step 5) with manual Cloudflare-for-SaaS at that point; automated certificate provisioning is a V2 item (TEN-05).

rows.q: Who may edit the terminology map: tenant admin or super admin only?
rows.note: Brand-control decision (the terminology map mechanism is TEN-32 V2 — the answer decides its scope too).

rows.q: Impersonation consent model: in-product consent per session or contract-level permission?
rows.note: Product/UX policy (the docs/21 view-as machinery supports both).

rows.q: What happens to existing data when a module entitlement is disabled, for example affiliate commissions after affiliate is turned off?
rows.note: Product semantics — disable = hide the surface, keep the data (the TEN-09 entitlement lifecycle exists; the data policy is product's).

rows.q: Do we support multiple brands or sub-tenants under one firm in V1? Expected answer is no.
rows.note: Scope call. Spec posture: one firm = one tenant (docs/47 multi-tenancy model); sub-tenants are a structural V2+ question.
